Inherited anticoagulant protein deficiency causes hypercoagulability. Thrombotic events are separately diagnosed complications; skin necrosis is treatment-related.
Chronic developmental and acquired lung injury defines BPD. Pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale are separate complications; diaphragmatic paralysis may be treatment-related.
Autonomous adrenal aldosterone excess produces the defining secondary hypertension and electrolyte disturbance; no additional common direct organ damage established.
Parathyroid hormone excess directly increases bone resorption; skeletal loss is common (~30%+ across primary and secondary forms). Renal disease may be causal or separately diagnosed.
CLL/SLL is a mature B-cell blood and lymphoid malignancy; lymphoma warrants the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Mature T-cell lymphoma arising around a breast implant; lymphoid malignancy supports both axes. Breast location supplies no additional axis.
Tumour originates in cutaneous apocrine sweat glands of the vulva, establishing dermatologic origin despite the vulvar location.
